# Cūḷagopālaka Sutta (MN 34 (PTS MN i 225))

**ID:** MN 34 (PTS MN i 225)
**Section:** Majjhimanikāya (mn)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-1
**Title (Pali):** Cūḷagopālaka Sutta
**PTS:** MN i 225
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0201m.mul3.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Cūḷagopālaka Sutta* ("The Shorter Discourse on the Cowherd") is the thirty-fourth discourse in the *Majjhimanikāya* [Bodhi 1995; Buswell & Lopez 2014]. Delivered by the Buddha while staying in the Vajjian territory at Ukkācelā on the banks of the Ganges River, the sutta centers on the extended simile of an inexperienced versus a wise cowherd guiding cattle across a river [Bodhi 1995; Rogell 2003; Buswell & Lopez 2014]. The Buddha explains that cattle led into the water at an improper ford by an unskillful cowherd meet with disaster and drown; likewise, practitioners who place their faith in teachers ignorant of this world and the hereafter, of Māra's realm, and of the realm of Death will suffer long-term harm [Bodhi 2012; Hazra 1994; Rogell 2003; Buswell & Lopez 2014]. Conversely, just as a wise cowherd chooses an appropriate ford so that all his cattle cross safely, those who follow the Buddha cross Māra's stream to the further shore of liberation [Bodhi 1995; Bodhi 2012; Rogell 2003]. The Buddha compares various categories of noble disciples reaching safety—from arahants down through stream-enterers and those following by Dhamma or faith—to different types of cattle crossing the current [Bodhi 1995; Nyanatusita 2013; Ohnuma 2007].

The sutta includes the formulation describing the attainment of the Deathless (*amatam adhigatam*) [Radich 2007]. In modern linguistic and chronological research, the discourse was assigned to a "middle" stratum in Kingsbury's statistical analysis of Pali aorist forms [Radich 2007].

 DharmaNexus corroborates these cross-language alignments with matching passages in the Chinese *Ekottarika-āgama* (T 125) and *Saṃyuktāgama* (T 99), while also recording weaker alignments with the *Patna Dharmapada* and the Tibetan translation of the *Buddhacarita* [DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali canon, DharmaNexus identifies 593 matching text-reuse segments across 58 canonical texts, sharing its most substantial passages with the *Sotāpatti Saṁyutta* (SN 55), the *Naḷakapāna Sutta* (MN 68), the *Tikanipāta* (AN 3), the *Mahāmālukya Sutta* (MN 64), and the *Catukkanipāta* (AN 4) [DharmaNexus].
